messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - elevated decode/stream OOM errors in eu-west-1 cluster (decode-family). Request drops ~28% in the last 4m. Auto-paging oncall.

miguel: oncall ack, joining bridge now -> https://meet.company/incident-1924001122

oncall-bot: Paging sara (oncall) via SMS. Escalation level 1.

sara: I'm on it. grabbing logs and metrics.

lee: spotting a config rollout 1924000600: streaming.max_tokens_policy=client_controlled. That seems suspicious.

sara: initial tail of decode pod log:
```
2026-03-15T10:45:03Z decode-2a9f: ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
2026-03-15T10:45:03Z req=xyz789 session=session-77 header:X-Requested-Max-Tokens=200000
2026-03-15T10:45:03Z action=drop response=backend_oom
```

miguel: confirm. looks like some sessions requested huge token budgets and the runtime kept growing KV cache until OOM. Any recent traffic pattern changes? We got a spike from acct:orion around 10:44.

infra_robin: infra note: several decode pods hit OOM and restarted, causing request routing to hit fewer nodes and amplify the failure.

sara: plan to mitigate: 1) emergency edge clamp to reject X-Requested-Max-Tokens > 16384 2) rollback the client_controlled policy 3) scale up decode nodes temporarily and drain flapping pods

miguel: doing step 1 now. Pushing edge rule via waf-api:
```
POST /waf/rules
{ "rule": "if header.X-Requested-Max-Tokens > 16384 then respond 400" }
```

lee: rolling back policy 1924000600 in config repo. deploying rollback to eu-west-1.

oncall-bot: sara acknowledged the page at 1924001130

sara: executing node draining + restart for pods failing OOM. kubectl drain pod/decode-2a9f --ignore-daemonsets; then delete pod to force new scheduler placement.

miguel: added temporary rate-limit at routing for acct:orion to 10 RPS to prevent big sessions from monopolizing GPUs.

cs_frontline: customer Orion reported session interruptions. Opening ticket ORION-112. I'll send an incident statement once we know the scope.

sara: metrics update: error-rate dropped to ~6% over 3m after edge clamp and rollback, but two pods still show high GPU memory before crash.

infra_robin: investigating crash log from one pod:
```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
  what():  CUDA out of memory
  backtrace:
   #0 decode_loop.cpp:398
   #1 decoder_worker.cpp:210
```
request headers snapshot:
```
X-Requested-Max-Tokens: 200000
X-Client-Id: acct:orion
```

miguel: root cause draft: config change enabled client-supplied max token budgets without a hard clamp. Some clients sent extremely large budgets -> KV-cache growth during streaming -> kernels allocated beyond GPU capacity -> CUDA OOMs -> pod restarts -> request drops.

lee: follow-ups to assign: CLAMP-101 - add hard clamp in HTTP edge + return 400, TEST-499 - integration test for header fuzzing, MON-720 - alert when GPU memory 95pct > 85% for 5m.

sara: I'm creating an incident hotfix branch to add HTTP clamp at edge and a runtime safe-guard in decode runtime to fail-fast on > 65536 tokens.

miguel: FYI I pushed a small hotfix to routing to backoff sessions over long-lived streaming to reduce KV cache growth. PR: https://git.company/infra/PR-912

oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled -> night oncall lee at 1924001200. Reminder will be sent in 1h.

cs_frontline: impact summary for CS: Orion had multiple dropped streams between 10:44-10:52 UTC. Other tenants saw 2-8% error spikes briefly. We're drafting customer comms and credit options.

infra_robin: action items: 1) implement MON-720 alert 2) add per-pod mem headroom panel 3) create playbook entry for runaway-streaming OOMs.

sara: quick note: we observed one malformed client that was replaying headers with X-Requested-Max-Tokens set to mammoth values due to a client SDK bug. Reached out to Orion eng.

miguel: will also add a canary that applies streaming config changes to 1% of traffic for 15m before global rollout.

lee: hotfix merged for HTTP clamp (400 response on >16384). Rolling out to edge now.

sara: after hotfix and rollback, error-rate back to baseline ~0.8%. Pods stable, memory headroom healthy.

miguel: suggest follow-up postmortem items: - permanent clamp at edge - config canary gating - per-GPU mem alert - integration test for header parsing - customer outreach and timeline

cs_frontline: Orion update: notified, asked for logs and timing. We'll include remediation steps and offer 2 weeks of service credit if they request.

sara: demobilizing primary responders. I'll draft the timeline and run a 90m post-incident sync tomorrow.

incident-bot: Incident marked mitigated at 1924001235. Postmortem draft: https://docs.company/incidents/1924001122-draft

miguel: thanks team. lessons learned: treat any client-configurable runtime param as untrusted by default. Gate with server-side limits.

lee: good work. :clap:
